pr_title: Fix expected argument count for `Callable` call errors
pr_comments: From a cursory look this seems sensible, but I'm surprised that it was wrong in so many places in the codebase. Is that due to an API design change that wasn't properly propagated?

> If we need to change the meaning of `argument`/`expected`, maybe this might need to be done via a new `GDExtensionCallError2` struct, preserving the compatibility for `GDExtensionCallError` uses somewhat

Hrm. If we wanted to make a new `GDExtensionCallError2`, then we'd need to also make new versions of every function that deals with `GDExtensionCallError`, which includes some function pointers that are used on _other_ structs, which would need new versions along with all the functions that accept those too. This quickly becomes quite a few changes.

Am I correct in understanding that this just affects the accuracy of some error messages? If so, the worst that could happen, is that a GDExtension compiled for Godot 4.1 but opened in Godot 4.2 could generate some incorrect error messages in some cases. This could maybe just be an acceptable weirdness with using older GDExtensions? It's not a crash, and it's not an error interpreted as a success or vice-versa.

We should also probably make changes similar to those in this PR to godot-cpp, so that it's using `argument` and `expected` correctly too.

> If we need to change the meaning of `argument`/`expected`, maybe this might need to be done via a new `GDExtensionCallError2` struct, preserving the compatibility for `GDExtensionCallError` uses somewhat. 

> Am I correct in understanding that this just affects the accuracy of some error messages? […] This could maybe just be an acceptable weirdness with using older GDExtensions? It's not a crash, and it's not an error interpreted as a success or vice-versa.
> 
> We should also probably make changes similar to those in this PR to godot-cpp, so that it's using `argument` and `expected` correctly too.

Here’s what this GDExtension user thinks. I say no needed, because
* This is a bug (within Godot Engine), not a feature (something intended according to documentation and/or intuition). See @dalexeev[’s comment](#issuecomment-1717302154)
  * My code actually has `error.expected ? error.expected : error.argument` to work this mistake around.
* You folks haven’t promised API stability yet. (e.g., #75779)

issue_context.title: Strange error message: "Method expected 0 arguments, but called with 0"
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot v4.1.1.stable

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Get strange error message "Method expected 0 arguments, but called with 0" while generating signal
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/52435334/2c3e2772-8a93-4ffc-b8f4-249ae342badd)
 

### Steps to reproduce

1. clone https://github.com/johnny-byte/godot_issue/tree/master
2. run
3. click mouse button right
4. get error message

### Minimal reproduction project

[BugScene.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/12388945/BugScene.zip)
comments:
I can confirm that the following error is printed with Godot version v4.2.dev3.official.013e8e3af when right-pressing the button from the attached zip minimal reproduction project:
```php
ERROR: Error calling from signal 'right_button_click' to callable: 'Control(Button.gd)::_on_my_color_picker_right_pressed': Method expected 0 arguments, but called with 0.
   at: emit_signalp (core/object/object.cpp:1084)
```

Your `emit()` does not provide the required argument.
But yeah, the error is strange.

review_comments: `expected` seems to be an enum value of `Variant::Type`.
